rules.title: Contraindicated Fluoroquinolone in Pediatric Patient (<18 Years)
rules.explanation: Fluoroquinolones are contraindicated in patients under 18 years due to established risk of cartilage erosion, permanent arthropathy, and weight-bearing joint injury.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Consider discussing age-appropriate first-line options: Amoxicillin for respiratory infections, ORS + Zinc for acute diarrhea, or Cefalexin for soft tissue infections. Verify local pediatric guidelines.

rules.title: Contraindicated Tetracycline in Pediatric Patient (<12 Years)
rules.explanation: Tetracyclines bind calcium in developing dentition, causing permanent tooth enamel hypoplasia and bone growth suppression.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Consider discussing beta-lactams or macrolides concordant with pediatric STGs.

rules.title: Contraindicated Antimicrobial in Pregnancy
rules.explanation: Prescribed agent carries established maternal/fetal risks (teratogenicity, ototoxicity, congenital skeletal defects, or cartilage erosion).
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Consider discussing safer pregnancy-category options: Amoxicillin, Cefalexin, or single-dose Fosfomycin (for lower UTI). Verify obstetric guidelines.

rules.title: Nitrofurantoin Contraindicated in Severe Renal Impairment (eGFR <30 mL/min)
rules.explanation: Nitrofurantoin requires adequate glomerular filtration to achieve therapeutic urinary concentrations. In eGFR <30 mL/min or geriatric impairment, drug accumulation causes treatment failure and severe peripheral neurotoxicity.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Consider discussing single-dose Fosfomycin (3g PO) or Cefalexin (500mg QID x 5d) for acute cystitis in renal impairment.

rules.title: Mandatory Renal Function Documentation Hold
rules.explanation: Narrow-therapeutic nephrotoxic agents require documented eGFR/creatinine clearance prior to administration to calculate dose adjustments and prevent acute tubular necrosis.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Document patient eGFR / Serum Creatinine before initiating narrow-therapeutic nephrotoxics.

rules.title: Potential Beta-Lactam Anaphylaxis / Cross-Reactivity Risk
rules.explanation: Patient has documented Penicillin / Beta-Lactam allergy. Administration carries risk of severe IgE-mediated anaphylaxis or cross-reactivity.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Consider discussing non-beta-lactam classes (e.g. Macrolides, Fosfomycin, or Doxycycline depending on indication). Confirm allergy severity.

rules.title: Regulatory Prohibited Fixed-Dose Combination (CDSCO Gazette Ban)
rules.explanation: Prescribed fixed-dose combination is banned by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) due to lack of therapeutic justification and accelerated resistance selection.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Discontinue dual FDC. Treat with single indicated first-line agent based on confirmed pathogen or standard guideline.

rules.title: Inappropriate Antimicrobial in Self-Limiting Viral Acute Bronchitis
rules.explanation: Acute bronchitis in immunocompetent patients is viral in >90% of cases. ICMR STG 2022 confirms antibiotics confer zero clinical benefit and increase adverse drug events.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Consider discussing symptomatic relief: hydration, steam inhalation, antitussives, and reassuring the patient regarding typical 10-14 day natural cough course.

rules.title: Inappropriate Antimicrobial in Viral Upper Respiratory Infection
rules.explanation: Common cold and non-streptococcal viral pharyngitis are exclusively viral. Empirical antibiotic therapy is contraindicated under ICMR and WHO stewardship standards.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Consider discussing supportive antipyretic care (Paracetamol), saline gargles, and rest.

rules.title: WHO AWaRe Reserve Escalation Alert for Mild Outpatient Infection
rules.explanation: Reserve-class antimicrobials are 'last-resort' agents reserved strictly for multidrug-resistant confirmed pathogens. Empirical outpatient use jeopardizes critical global antimicrobial reserves.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Consider discussing Access-group standard first-line therapy (e.g. Nitrofurantoin or Fosfomycin for UTI; Amoxicillin for mild CAP).

rules.title: Excessive Prescribed Treatment Duration (>5 Days)
rules.explanation: ICMR STG 2022 standard recommends short-course therapy (3 to 5 days) for uncomplicated cystitis and mild CAP. Extended courses select for resistant commensal flora without improving clinical cure.
rules.guideline_discussion_prompt: Consider discussing 5-day treatment completion if patient is clinically afebrile.

EVID_ICMR_PED_FQ.title: ICMR Standard Treatment Guidelines: Pediatric Antimicrobial Stewardship
EVID_ICMR_PED_FQ.excerpt: Fluoroquinolones (Ciprofloxacin, Ofloxacin, Levofloxacin) are strictly contraindicated in pediatric patients (<18 years) due to documented animal and clinical evidence of cartilage erosion, arthropathy, and tendon rupture, except in specific life-threatening multidrug-resistant cystic fibrosis or anthrax.

EVID_ICMR_PED_TETRA.title: ICMR Guidelines: Pediatric Contraindications for Tetracyclines
EVID_ICMR_PED_TETRA.excerpt: Tetracyclines form a stable calcium complex in any bone-forming tissue. Use during tooth development causes permanent tooth discoloration (yellow-gray-brown) and enamel hypoplasia in children under 12 years.

EVID_WHO_PREG_ANTIBIOTICS.title: WHO Clinical Guidelines on Antibiotic Safety in Pregnancy and Lactation
EVID_WHO_PREG_ANTIBIOTICS.excerpt: Fluoroquinolones, Tetracyclines, and Aminoglycosides carry proven fetal toxicity risks (cartilage lesions, permanent bone/dental hypoplasia, and 8th cranial nerve damage). They must not be prescribed during pregnancy unless no viable alternative exists.

EVID_BEERS_ICMR_NITROFURANTOIN.title: AGS Beers Criteria & ICMR Guidelines: Nitrofurantoin in Renal Impairment
EVID_BEERS_ICMR_NITROFURANTOIN.excerpt: Avoid nitrofurantoin in individuals with creatinine clearance / eGFR < 30 mL/min. Inadequate urinary drug concentration occurs alongside increased risk of severe peripheral neuropathy and pulmonary fibrosis.

EVID_KDIGO_RENAL_HOLD.title: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury & Drug Dosing
EVID_KDIGO_RENAL_HOLD.excerpt: Prior to administering narrow-therapeutic index nephrotoxic agents including Aminoglycosides, Polymyxins, and Glycopeptides, baseline renal function (eGFR or Serum Creatinine) must be documented to guide initial interval and dosage titration.

EVID_ICMR_ALLERGY_ANAPHYLAXIS.title: ICMR Guidelines: Antimicrobial Hypersensitivity and Cross-Reactivity
EVID_ICMR_ALLERGY_ANAPHYLAXIS.excerpt: Patients with severe or unknown Penicillin hypersensitivity must not be prescribed Aminopenicillins or early-generation Cephalosporins without specialist immunological allergy clearance due to the risk of fatal anaphylaxis.

EVID_CDSCO_BANNED_FDC.title: CDSCO Gazette Notification: Banned Irrational Fixed-Dose Combinations
EVID_CDSCO_BANNED_FDC.excerpt: The Central Government hereby prohibits the manufacture, sale, and distribution of irrational antimicrobial combinations including Cefixime + Azithromycin and Ofloxacin + Ornidazole as they lack therapeutic justification and accelerate antimicrobial resistance.

EVID_ICMR_RESP_BRONCHITIS.title: ICMR STG 2022: Respiratory Infections — Acute Bronchitis
EVID_ICMR_RESP_BRONCHITIS.excerpt: Acute bronchitis in immunocompetent adults is predominantly viral and self-limiting. Antibiotics provide zero clinical benefit and are not indicated. Symptomatic management alone is standard of care.

EVID_ICMR_URTI_COLD.title: ICMR STG 2022: Upper Respiratory Infections & Common Cold
EVID_ICMR_URTI_COLD.excerpt: Common cold, viral rhinopharyngitis, and non-streptococcal pharyngitis are viral etiologies. Antibiotic therapy is contraindicated; antipyretics and supportive hydration represent first-line therapy.

EVID_WHO_AWARE_2023.title: WHO AWaRe Antibiotic Classification & Stewardship Book 2023
EVID_WHO_AWARE_2023.excerpt: Reserve group antibiotics such as Meropenem, Linezolid, and Colistin should be treated as last-resort options. Their use should be strictly restricted to highly specific patients and settings with confirmed or strongly suspected MDR infections.

EVID_ICMR_SHORT_COURSE.title: ICMR Standard Treatment Guidelines: Optimal Antimicrobial Duration
EVID_ICMR_SHORT_COURSE.excerpt: For uncomplicated acute cystitis and mild outpatient community-acquired pneumonia, evidence-based antimicrobial duration is 3 to 5 days. Prolonged therapy does not enhance clinical cure and directly induces collateral resistance in host microbiota.
